data.cultural_impact: In Islamic culture, the name Suhayl is considered to be of Arabic origin and means "big mountain," but it is also connected to the bright star, Canopus, which is one of the dwelling places of one of the seventy thousand Angels of Allah. This celestial body is believed to guide lost sailors and travelers in the desert. Additionally, the mention of Suhayl is found in the hadiths, where Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) spoke about the arrival of the Antichrist and the signs that will precede his coming. According to these hadiths, the arrival of the Antichrist will be preceded by the emergence of many false Masihs and Messiahs. One of them will be called Dabbat Suhayl, meaning the foal of Suhayl, and it will appear from the direction of Syria. This shows the importance of Suhayl in Islamic history and culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, Suhayl is a symbol of guidance and illumination, as represented by the star of the same name. It is believed that Allah (SWT) takes care of His creation through various Signs and Symbols in the universe, and Suhayl is one of them. This star is used as a symbol of hope, guidance, and protection against the darkness of ignorance and misguidance. Muslims believe that seeking knowledge, truth, and guidance from Allah and through the verses of the Qur'an, as well as following the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), are the paths that lead to illumination and guidance. Thus, the name Suhayl carries a spiritual significance of encouraging individuals to follow the true path of guidance, as symbolized by the bright star.
